cover.main: SOUTH FLORIDA SIBLINGS' SUBWAY VENDOR SCHEME COST

slides.headline: Feds say Subway vendor scheme cost about $80M
slides.body: Federal prosecutors say a South Florida sibling duo steered Subway franchisees into preferred vendors tied to kickbacks, costing owners about $80 million.

photo.query: Subway restaurant exterior sign strip mall Florida
photo.prompt: low-angle photo of a Subway sign on a Florida strip mall storefront with dramatic late-day shadows, no people visible

slides.headline: The siblings were federally charged Thursday
slides.body: The case was announced Thursday, Oct. 1. Prosecutors describe it as an alleged Subway franchise kickback and bribery scheme.

photo.query: federal courthouse Miami Florida exterior flags
photo.prompt: dramatic exterior of a federal courthouse in South Florida with U.S. flags, courthouse steps and heavy shadows, no people visible

slides.headline: Prosecutors say owners had to use preferred vendors
slides.body: Prosecutors say Subway restaurant owners were forced to use preferred vendors as part of the alleged kickback scheme.

slides.headline: The indictment says franchisees were targeted
slides.body: The indictment describes an alleged $80 million bribery scheme targeting Subway restaurant owners.

slides.headline: A Pinecrest woman is part of the case
slides.body: A Pinecrest woman was charged in the $80 million Subway kickback case, tying the federal case directly to Miami-Dade.
